note: Version lock for the expense policy document. Each entry pins one version string to the OCF-1 digest of the document that carried it: sha256(utf8("outpocket/policy/1" + U+000A + canonical form)). tests/policy-lock.test.mjs recomputes the digest of the shipped document and asserts the pair is present here. Effect: a limit cannot move without the version moving, the version cannot move without the document moving, and a retired version number cannot be reused for different content. This is the mechanical half of demo beat 1.

versions.note: The document in policy.schema.json examples[0]. Ported from countinghouse/src/policy.js with two required changes: FX rates become integer micro-USD, and every fix string is rewritten to pass violation.schema.json x-fixLint.

versions.derivation: Byte-identical to 2026-08.1 except three values: version becomes "2026-08.2", effective_from becomes "2026-08-29", and limits_cents.transport_per_line becomes 5000 (from 15000). Nothing else changes. The implementer MUST produce exactly this document; if the recomputed digest differs, something else moved too. Changing the limit ALONE gives sha256:17bc4b2d1031b63e07a3983b067c8485316e8c16b53454e481680f65b7962e92; if your recomputation lands there, you did not bump the version. The byte count is 2457, one LESS than 2026-08.1's 2458: version and effective_from keep their lengths and 15000 shortens to 5000. It was published as 2458 until 2026-08-28, which would have failed tests/policy-lock.test.mjs on the demo policy - that is, on demo beat 1 itself.
versions.note: This is the policy finance switches to during demo beat 1. Dropping the transport cap from $150 to $50 makes a line that validated a moment ago fail, which is why the same agent's next attempt is refused without anything about the agent changing.
